title: Handoff & Observability Matrix for PRs (personal scratchpad)
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad mapping out what needs to happen immediately after merging medium-to-large PRs that touch the serving runtime, routing, or caching layers. Goal is to reduce churn from ambiguous ownership and missing observability during the first 48h after deploys.

Context: 
- Too many recent incidents where a change that looked safe locally caused degraded tail latency because there was no canary metric or dashboard.
- Hand-offs to SRE/owners are often verbal in Slack and not captured in ticket or runbooks.

High-level checklist (first 48h):
- [ ] Post a short summary comment on the merged PR with: deployed commit SHA, region(s), expected impact, why change was made, quick rollback steps.
- [ ] Create/attach a short runbook snippet to the PR (1-2 bullets) and link the oncall rotation.
- [ ] Add canary and fallback alerts for the affected routes (p50, p95, p99; error rate).
- [ ] Confirm trace sampling is enabled for the release window and verify one successful sampled trace for a new code path.
- [ ] Schedule a brief FYI in #serving-runtime for the next 24hrs with the PR link and owners.

Handoff matrix (who does what) - quick reference:
- Author: write the PR summary + rollback command + update PR description with runbook snippet.
- Primary reviewer: confirm canary metrics & dashboard links are present in PR.
- SRE oncall: enable increased trace sampling and monitor p99 for 2 windows.
- Product owner: sanity-check user-impact statement (if customer-visible).

Observability artifacts to add (minimum):
- Dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), success rate, rate of token generation/second if applicable.
- Traces: at least one span with the new handler name/tag and KV cache hit/miss tag.
- Logs: structured log key: "pr_deploy_id" and include commit SHA and deploy region.
- Metrics: a boolean gauge "new_handler_enabled" (0/1) for quick detection if rollout didn't complete.

Proposed canary alert thresholds (example starting points):
- p99 latency > baseline + 40% for 10m -> SEV3
- error rate > baseline + 1% absolute AND request volume > 100r/min -> SEV2
- new handler error count > 5 in 5min -> SEV2

Automation ideas (cheap wins):
- 1) PR template checkbox group that autogenerates a runbook snippet (author fills the short answers -> template builds snippet).
- 2) GitHub action that posts a synthesized summary to #serving-runtime on merge (includes links to dashboards inferred from modified routes).
- 3) Small infra script that tags traces/logs for this deploy window (cronjob + temporary env var).

Immediate follow-ups (tickets I should create after merging a large PR):
- Create RLW ticket "observability: dashboard for <route>" (owner: primary reviewer)
- Create small task to add structured log keys and update docs (owner: author)
- Create test in e2e suite simulating high-concurrency prefix to catch p99 regressions (owner: QA lead)

Risk matrix quick sketch (for triage):
- Low risk: config-only change, no runtime path -> quick merge, no canary needed unless config affects routing.
- Medium risk: touch to routing/handler selection/cache invalidation -> add canary + 24h monitor.
- High risk: change touching KV cache semantics, kernel selection, or batching logic -> require canary + manual approval from SRE + rollback plan + load-test window.

Example snippet to paste in PR description (short):
---
Deploy notes:
- Commit: $COMMIT_SHA
- Regions: us-west1, eu-central1
- Expected impact: reduces cold-start for handler X; unlikely to increase latency but changes cache key shape for backend Y.
- Rollback: revert to tag vX.Y (git revert <sha> && deploy) OR scale old pool to 0->1 (runbook link).
- Monitoring: dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/board/serving-runtime?var-route=X
---

Quick debugging commands (for oncall):
- curl -H 'X-Debug:1' https://api.redwood/route/X?input=test  # force trace
- redis-cli --latency -h cache-host  # quick health check of KV layer
- rli run traces --filter commit:$COMMIT_SHA --last 1h  # (internal CLI)

Notes to self (open questions):
- Should we add a standardized "canary window" label in PRs so alerts automatically escalate based on how long the code is in canary?
- How do we best handle feature-flag partial rollouts that change cache key semantics (tie to rollout percent?)

Next steps for me:
- Iterate the PR template (add runbook snippet generator) -> draft task today.
- Prototype a lightweight GitHub action to post merge summaries (P0 prototype next week).
- Run a small pair-debug session with SRE to agree on alert thresholds for routing changes.

Scratchpad end. Keep this lean and copy into PRs when needed.

References / quick links:
- Serving runtime PR example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4271
- Related Jira: RLW-1984
- Console PR with dashboard changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1290

-- Ananya
